description: The plot titled “Massive Activation of baseline” illustrates how the maximum activation value varies across model layers for multiple components. The x-axis is labeled “Layer” and uses a linear scale, spanning approximately layers 0 through 23 with major tick labels shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Max Activation Value” on a linear scale, ranging from 0 up to about 1600 with regularly spaced tick labels every 200 units. Four lines are shown: a blue dashed line (legend entry not visible) stays near 0 for most layers and then rises late, reaching roughly ~250 by the final layer; an orange dotted line labeled “attn_residual” is near 0 through about layer 4, jumps to around ~1400 at about layer 6, remains near ~1500–1600 through roughly layers 14–21, and then drops sharply near the end to a few hundred by the last layer; a green dash-dot line labeled “ffn_output” is near 0 early, spikes to about ~1400 around layer 5, falls back close to 0 by around layers 7–11, shows another spike around layer 13 near ~700, returns to low values through the mid-to-late teens, and then spikes again near layer 22 to around ~1200 before dropping again by the final layer; a red solid line labeled “ffn_residual” is near 0 through about layer 4, rises sharply to about ~1400 at layer ~5, increases to roughly ~1500 by around layer 7, stays near ~1500 through about layer 12, steps up to around ~1580–1600 around layers 14–21, and then drops steeply near layer 22 to roughly ~400 before ending around ~600 at the last layer.
